newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK stocks close sharply down on property concerns.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks close sharply down on property concerns.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks closed Tuesday sharply lower after setting a new intra-day high in the morning, driven down by worries about the outlook for the property market and disappointment in the government land auction, broker said.

"Expectations were out of the ballpark," said Angus Shillington in institutional sales at Asia Equity after the auction's first site went at a price well below forecasts. "Disappointment was inevitable."
The Hang Seng Index closed 230.73 points or 1.54 percent lower at 14,760.17. Turnover was a very robust HK$23.27 billion, although less than Monday's record turnover of HK$26.48 billion.
In the morning, the index rose to set an all-time high of 15,020.96, chiefly on continued covering of warrants issued the previous day, brokers said.
"Trading houses were the main players today," said Steve Lindsay in derivatives sales at HSBC James Capel.
In the afternoon, the index fell sharply to a day's low of 14,607.18 points, jittery over the low HK$5.5 billion winning bid for the Stanley site in the government land auction.

The second site in Hunghom was taken by a higher than expected HK$6.06 billion bid, but after the stock market closed. Cheung Kong, which took the Hunghom site with a winning bid of HK$6.06 billion, compared with expectations of HK$4 billion to HK$5 billion, was keen to get it, said Shillington.
Cheung Kong closed HK$2.50 lower at HK$77.75 and subsidiary Hutchison Whampoa, which will be a partner in the development, fell HK$1.00 to HK$64.25.

Paliburg, which closed HK$0.05 down at HK$10.15, and China Overseas Land which ended HK$0.10 weaker at HK$5.65, bought the first auction site for HK$5.5 billion, well below the forecast HK$6.4 billion to HK$7.3 billion.
Banking giant HSBC Holdings slid HK$6.00 to HK$227.00 on very heavy turnover of HK$1.36 billion.
"There has been a change in theme," said Lindsay.
The buying interest in HSBC by London-based institutions is drying up, and there is a need now to rebalance Hong Kong portfolio weightings, he said.
CITIC Pacific went against the trend, rising to an all time high of HK$48.30 then easing to close HK$1.50 higher at HK$47.40 on heavy turnover of HK$880 million.
Red chip newcomer Beijing Enterprises lost HK$2.75 to HK$51.50 on heavy turnover of HK$1.42 billion.
